subject.title: Feature: Reason-aware cron guardrails (quota/auth/rate-limit aware backoff + circuit breaker)

question: Should recurring cron jobs pause automatically on definitive billing, permanent-authentication, and format failures by default, and if so after what threshold and recovery rule?
rationale: This changes established scheduler defaults and can intentionally stop existing automation while adding persisted state and operator-recovery semantics that implementation evidence alone cannot safely choose.

options.title: Built-in guarded defaults
options.body: Pause after a small reason-specific threshold, reuse existing retry and failure-alert configuration where possible, and require explicit resume after billing, authentication, or format recovery.

options.title: Opt-in strict guard
options.body: Preserve current recurring behavior by default and add an explicit strict policy for operators who want automatic pausing.

options.title: Alerts and cooldowns only
options.body: Keep jobs enabled indefinitely and rely on provider cooldowns, generic backoff, and failure notifications without a job-level circuit breaker.

recommendation.title: Built-in guarded defaults
recommendation.body: Pause after a small reason-specific threshold, reuse existing retry and failure-alert configuration where possible, and require explicit resume after billing, authentication, or format recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest review and adjacent cron history make this person the strongest available routing candidate for the scheduler-default decision.
